chunks: And by this chain, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there are one hundred and twenty mercies around the Kaaba. From these, sixty are for the circumambulators, forty for the praying ones, and twenty for the beholders.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Kaaba, the cubic building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the distribution of divine mercy around the Kaaba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi quantifies the spiritual rewards of the Kaaba, distinguishing between the active worship of Tawaf and prayer and the passive merit of contemplation (Nazr). In Shia scholarship, this highlights the Kaaba not merely as a structural focal point but as a locus of divine grace where even visual engagement yields significant spiritual benefit, reinforcing the concept of the House as a 'place of return' and mercy.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High has one hundred and twenty Mercies around the Kabah. From these, sixty are for the circumambulators, and forty for the Praying ones, and twenty for the beholders’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, has one hundred twenty blessings around al-Ka’bah of which sixty are for those who perform Tawaf, forty for those who perform salat (prayer) and twenty for those who look at al-Ka’bah.’”
